{{Quote|We have thousands of probe droids searching the galaxy. I want proof, not leads!|[[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Kendal Ozzel/Legends|Kendal Ozzel]]|audio=Ozzel-ProbeDroids.flac|<ref name="ESB">{{Film|V}}</ref>}}
The '''Viper probe droid''', commonly referred to as the '''probot''' or '''Imperial probe droid''', was a deep-[[Realspace/Legends|space]] exploration and reconnaissance [[Probe droid/Legends|probe droid]] produced by [[Arakyd Industries/Legends|Arakyd Industries]]. A member of the [[Arakyd Probot Series]], the Viper model was based on the success of [[Galalloy Industries]]' early probe [[Droid/Legends|droids]]. The design of the probot also relied heavily on the work of [[Viper Sensor Intelligence Systems]], a corporation acquired by Arakyd during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. Though they were used almost exclusively by the military, they were considered [[Class two droid/Legends|class two]] [[Explorer droid/Legends|exploration droids]].

==Specifications==
{{Quote|'Fraid there's not much left."<br />"What was it?"<br />"A droid of some kind. I didn't hit it that hard. It must've had a self-destruct.|audio=Solo-Organa-Probedroid.flac|Han Solo and [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Princess Leia]]|<ref name="ESB" />}}
[[File:ProbeDroid_egvv.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Viper probe droid [[:Category:Technical drawing images|schematics]].]]
[[Crab/Legends|Crab]]-[[Limb/Legends|legged]] and [[Spider/Legends|spider]]-[[Eye/Legends|eyed]], the Viper [[Probe droid/Legends|probe droid]] was an improved and refined version of the [[Prowler 1000 seeker droid/Legends|Prowler 1000 seeker droid]].<ref name="The Droids of Episode III">{{InsiderCite|81|The Droids of Episode III: It's a Junkyard Smackdown!}}</ref> Lightly-armored, it measured 1.6 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in height with five manipulator arms extending from a central pod and several retractable [[Sensor/Legends|sensor]] arms for gathering samples. High resolution receivers and sensors covered the domed head&mdash;including motion, acoustic, sonic, and seismic sensors, a radiation meter, magnetic imager, and [[Holocamera/Legends|holocamera]]. It had an [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] sensor capable of determining a [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] atmosphere class within one half-hour. It moved on a [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] generator which was equipped to operate over any terrain.<ref name="GG3" /> One of the arms was high-torque, and the droid was equipped with a floodlight on its head.<ref name="RS II guide">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader: The Official Nintendo Player's Guide]]''</ref> In addition, when making transmissions, the probe droid emitted a audio encrypted Imperial computer code set of an unknown serial number.

Information was relayed back to its superiors via a high-frequency [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]] transceiver. Its repulsorlift engines carried the droid across terrain at up to 40 km/h, while the arms gathered samples. Vipers were delivered to their targets through single-use custom built [[Probe-Mate hyperspace pod|hyperspace pods]]. They were commonly deployed along the perimeters of key strategic [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] and [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]] to act as automated guardians.<ref name="GG3" />

Typically, a Viper probe droid cost 14,500 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]].<ref name="GG3" /> They were capable of being deployed from Galactic Empire [[Command center]]s.<ref name="SW:GB">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref>

==History==
[[File:Viper_probe_droid_and_Quarren.jpg|thumb|left|170px|A [[Quarren/Legends|Quarren]] evades a Viper probe droid.]]
Arakyd probe droids were originally designed for use by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] in survey and exploration duty.<ref name="GG3" /> Some droids were applied to military uses; for example, the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] employed a number of upgraded probots during the [[Battle of Kashyyyk/Legends|invasion]] of [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]] during the Clone Wars.<ref name="Deep Forest" /> With the fall of the Republic and the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], Arakyd produced new modified versions of their probots with military-level sensors and equipment and marketed them as Viper probe droids.<ref name="GG3" /> 

===The Empire's probing eyes===
[[File:AnoatCity-DFRemaster.png|thumb|right|200px|Kyle Katarn shoots a hovering Viper probe droid guarding the area of the [[Mission to Anoat|Anoat sewers]].]]
Viper probots in service with the Empire were upgraded under the direct supervision of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] and featured a [[Blaster cannon/Legends|blaster cannon]], a [[Self-destruct mechanism/Legends|self-destruct mechanism]], and, in some cases, [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]].<ref name="GG3" /> These armed probe droids formed part of the security/defensive force of various bases of the Galactic Empire, such as [[Gromas Mines]], [[Imperial Detention Center]], the area around the [[Imperial Security Operations]] building in the [[Galactic City/Legends|Imperial City]], even inside the ''[[Executor/Legends|Executor]]''. Moff [[Rebus]] employed some droids as security for his hideout in [[Anoat City]], including probe droids. Rebel [[agent/Legends|agent]] [[Kyle Katarn]] dealt with those droids while [[Mission to Anoat|sabotaging]] the [[Dark Trooper Project]].<ref name="Dark Forces Official Player's Guide">''[[Dark Forces Official Player's Guide]]''</ref> 

The droids also saw wide service with the [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence's]] [[Analysis Bureau (Imperial Intelligence)|Analysis Bureau]], which used them as remote surveillance droids posted largely in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. In conflict zones, probots often worked alongside the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] to monitor traffic and provide early warnings of attack.<ref name="GG3" /> 

Shortly after the [[Battle of Tatooine (Galactic Civil War)|Battle of Tatooine]], the Empire dispatched probe droids to [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] in an attempt to recover the stolen plans for the Death Star.<ref name="SW1991">[[Star Wars (1991 video game)|''Star Wars'' video game (1991)]]</ref> [[0 ABY/Legends|Six]] [[Standard month/Legends|months]] after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the Galactic Empire sent a detachment of probe droids to [[Ambush at Mos Eisley|root out]] Rebel [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]. They were destroyed by Skywalker and [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]].<ref name="SW:RS">[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']]</ref> Probe droids were also used to scout ahead for Imperial strike forces, including during the [[Reytha campaign]]<ref name="SW:GB" /> and the [[Battle of Corellia (1 ABY)|battle at Corellia]], or were sent on search [[Search for the Nonnah|missions]] like at [[Chorax]].<ref name="SW:RS" /> Several were also dispatched to [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]] as security measures while the Imperials arrived on the planet to [[Mission to Dantooine|detain]] the defecting Imperial officer [[Tycho Celchu/Legends|Tycho Celchu]].<ref name="RSIII">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''</ref>

Following the [[Evacuation of Yavin]], the Empire commissioned thousands of probe droids to scour [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] for hidden [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] bases.<ref name="GG3" /> This large new line of Viper droids was manufactured on [[Mechis III/Legends|Mechis III]]. Darth Vader personally oversaw the project from the start, visiting the manufacturing facility<ref name="IG-88" /> and assigning ships of his [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron]] to deploy them into the far reaches of space.<ref name="ESB" /> The overall military and political goal was to pin down the elusive and mobile [[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance High Command]].<ref name="GG3" /> Vader himself was obsessed above all with hunting down [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]].<ref name="ESB" /> He transmitted special orders that the probes be programmed to prioritize both Skywalker and the ''[[Millennium Falcon/Legends|Millennium Falcon]],'' [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo's]] starship.<ref name="Freedom's Winter">{{ESBRadio|Freedom's Winter}}</ref>

The Empire's success with the Arakyd's military model of the Viper yielded plans for the [[C-Viper series|C-Viper probe droid]], a more streamlined variant designed for planetary law enforcement organizations.<ref name="News 14">{{JournalCite|14|Galaxywide NewsNets}}</ref>

===Eyes and ears of the revolution===
{{Quote|Go and report. You have much to see. Burn brightly.|IG-88, to the last Viper probe droid constructed on Mechis III|<ref name="IG-88" />}}
[[File:Viper_probe_droid.jpg|thumb|200px|left|A Viper probe droid enters a cave.]]
When Darth Vader commissioned the construction of thousands of Viper probe droids on Mechis III, he was unaware that the rogue [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droid]] [[IG-88A/Legends|IG-88]] had [[Mechis III Uprising|taken control]] of the planet's automated factories. IG-88 was slowly developing plans for a [[Droid Revolution]] in which the droids of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] would rise up together and seize power from organic life. Vader's visit to Mechis was in fact the closest the conspiracy ever came to being discovered; but the IG droids masked their purpose well, and Vader only sensed a slight disturbance whose source he could not pinpoint.<ref name="IG-88" />

Vader impressed IG-88, both for the raw power he commanded and his blending of organic and mechanical traits. IG-88 decided to use Vader and his commissioned line of probe droids as an integral part of his plan. He gave them a secondary set of programming. They received the same [[sentience programming]] that the IG-88 droids had themselves, and they became clandestine solders in [[IG-88's Droid Army|his Droid Army]]. As they went about their missions for the Empire, they were to secretly relay their intelligence back to Mechis III. Thus, they simultaneously served as the eyes and ears of the revolution. Through them, IG-88 would learn about the Empire's plans, actions and vulnerabilities. Eventually, the droids planned to appropriate the Empire's power and make it their own.<ref name="IG-88" />

===Finding Echo Base===
{{Quote|I think we've got something, sir. The report is only a fragment from a probe droid in the Hoth system, but it's the best lead we've had.|[[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Firmus Piett/Legends|Firmus Piett]], to Admiral Kendal Ozzel|<ref name="ESB" />}}
[[File:Arakyd_Viper.jpg|thumb|200px|right|The Viper on Hoth searches for Echo Base.]]
[[Unidentified probe droid (Hoth)|One Arakyd Viper]], launched from a [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] of Death Squadron,<ref name="Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> landed on the ice planet [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] as part of Vader's galaxy-wide search for the hidden Rebel base.<ref name="ESB" /> After it emerged from its hyperspace pod, the probe droid detected a faint comm signal and began to travel toward its probable destination point. The next morning it approached the Rebels' [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]]. It detected the base's large [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|deflector shield generator]] and began to record it, transmitting the information to [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]], the [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']]. It went on to map out other features of Echo Base and its defenses, information that would be critical for the Empire in the coming battle.<ref name="GG3" /> IG-88, back on Mechis III, received the same information. [[IG-88B/Legends|IG-88B]] traveled to Hoth to observe and learn from Vader's subsequent actions.<ref name="IG-88" />

[[Sentry marker|Warning sensors]] placed by [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] had already picked up traces of the probe, alerting the Rebels to the presence of an unidentified object.<ref name="The Coming Storm">{{ESBRadio|The Coming Storm}}</ref> The droid was next detected by a [[Unidentified Rebel trooper (Station 3-8)|lone trooper]] in [[Station 3-8]]; it destroyed the station with its blaster before the trooper could see what it was.<ref name="ESB Novel">[[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back'' novelization]]</ref> Solo and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] were dispatched to the nearby [[Ceyan Range/Legends|Ceyan Range]].<ref name="ItWoSWT">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]''</ref> The probe detected their approach but was no match for them. While Chewbacca acted as a decoy, Solo blasted the confused droid from the other direction.<ref name="GG3" /> Seeing that it was cornered, the droid activated its self-destruct mechanism to avoid capture.<ref name="ESB" />

The Rebels realized they had been discovered and prepared to evacuate. On the ''Executor,'' Admiral [[Kendal Ozzel/Legends|Kendal Ozzel]] dismissed the idea that the probe's fragmentary data proved anything, but Vader was confident that the droid had discovered the hidden Rebel base. Death Squadron proceeded to Hoth and launched a [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|full-scale ground assault]], which occupied the base and scattered the Rebels.<ref name="ESB" /> Several Viper probes went as scouts ahead of the main force. A few Rebel [[Snowspeeder/Legends|snowspeeders]] engaged them in combat in the initial phase of the battle.<ref name="Shadows game">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (video game)|''Shadows of the Empire'' video game]]</ref> One probot, separated from the rest of the invasion force, was attacked by a wampa and stashed in its cave like other prey.<ref name="Fact File Wampa">[[The Official Star Wars Fact File 51|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' 51:]] "Hoth - Wampa Ice Cave"</ref>

===Later use===
After the Battle of Hoth, Arakyd and the Empire cooperated to produce the [[Infiltrator probe droid]], a new version of the Viper designed to sabotage and seize control of a starship.<ref name="Comic 45">[[Star Wars (1977) 45|''Star Wars'' (1977) 45]]</ref>

The would-be droid revolution, which involved numerous Viper probes as co-conspirators, was snuffed out in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]]. [[IG-88A/Legends|IG-88A]] installed his droid consciousness into the computer core of the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]] as a final preparatory step. IG-88 was to send out a signal to droids everywhere, including the line of Viper probe droids, to rise up and turn on their masters. But the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] ended with the Death Star destroyed and the planned revolution in shambles.<ref name="IG-88" /> 

As the Empire lost ground to the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], it continued to make use of Viper probe droids. In [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]], [[Jerec (Inquisitor)|Jerec]] and his [[Vengeance Battle Group]], discovered [[Ruusan/Legends|Ruusan]] and sent several probe droids before [[Battle of Fort Nowhere|his invasion]]. The battle group used more heavily-armed probe droids boasting four energy cannons, one at each side.<ref name="JK">''[[Dark Forces: Jedi Knight]]''</ref>

The [[Dark Empire|Empire Reborn]] developed the [[Hunter-Killer probot]], a variant of the Viper probe droid scaled up to a colossal size that could operate as an autonomous patrol ship.<ref name="Dark Empire 5">[[Dark Empire 5|''Dark Empire'' 5]]</ref> In [[14 ABY/Legends|14 ABY]] the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Jaden Korr]] encountered probe droids used by the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] on his [[Mission to Hoth (Jaden Korr)|scouting mission]] on Hoth.<ref name="JK:JA" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:MCQ-probedroid.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Probe droid concept art by [[Ralph McQuarrie]].]]
The [[Unidentified probe droid (Hoth)|probe droid that landed on Hoth]] was created for [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars:'' Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']] and first appeared in the [[1980]] [[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|novelization]] by [[Donald F. Glut]]. [[Ralph McQuarrie]] designed the droid, inspired by artwork by [[W:Jean Giraud|Jean "Moebius" Giraud]]. Later Star Wars films also share many visual characteristics with Giraud's work, particularly the depiction of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].<ref name="Still Designing">{{InsiderCite|24|Still Designing A Galaxy Far, Far Away: A Profile of "Artiste Extraordinaire" Ralph McQuarrie|Still Designing A Galaxy Far, Far Away: A Profile of 'Artiste Extraordinaire' Ralph McQuarrie}}</ref> The film ''THX 1138'' features numerous radio voices that sound strikingly similar to and likely influenced the strange electronic voice of the probe droid in ''The Empire Strikes Back''.

Artists created two models of the probe droid for the film. One was life-sized and appeared in the scene where the droid fights against Han Solo and Chewbacca. It ran on tracks in the snow to simulate its hovering movement. The scene was shot on location in [[Finse]], Norway. A dynamite explosion served to portray its meteoric landing on the surface of Hoth. A second model was used to portray the droid emerging from its landing site. This model, made by [[Joe Johnston]], was filmed against a miniature set at [[Industrial Light & Magic]].<ref name="Making Of">''[[The Making of The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref> The Arakyd Viper was first identified by name in ''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]],'' published by [[West End Games]] in [[1987]].

''[[Star Wars: Rebellion: Prima's Official Strategy Guide]]'' explains that Imperial probe droids are equipped with small hyperdrives, enabling them to scout the galaxy without needing to be deployed by capital ships, for use in the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']]. This serves as the game-mechanics explanation for the absence of the Predator I Probe-Mate jump pod in ''Star Wars: Rebellion'', which is the Viper probe droid's mode of hyperspace transportation.

Probe droids also appear in the [[2006]] video game ''[[LEGO Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy]]'', a humorous take on the [[original trilogy]] in LEGO form. The game is also included in its [[2007]] [[LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga|compilation re-release]].

It should be noted that the main image used on this article is a picture of the damaged model from the [[Lucasfilm Archives]], with its right antenna bent slightly to the left.
